title: Humility
tomorrow: ten men are healed. why does only one come back?

cards: In a lot of group photos, someone angles for the middle. Luke says that at the same dinner, Jesus watched the guests choosing out the chief rooms, the best seats.
So he told them a parable: at a wedding, don't take the top seat, or someone more honored may arrive and the host will ask you to move down, with everyone watching. Sit lower instead.
Then the host may come and say, “Friend, go up higher.”

teach.h: SIT LOWER: FRIEND, GO UP HIGHER.
teach.b: He ends with a line that flips the seating chart: “For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.”
Peter turns it into clothing: “be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.” Clothed: not a mood that comes and goes, but something put on each morning.
Philippians names the fabric: “in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” Humility here isn't hating yourself. The guest in the parable is still called friend.

teach.h: THE WEEK TAKES THE LOWER SEAT.
teach.b: It's taking the lower seat freely, and making room. A new stretch of the path, the heart, starts today, and it starts low on purpose. Now look back at the week.
The earth is his, not ours. A city's good above your own side. Justice that hears the other camp.
Truth said so someone else can grow.
Peace begun from your own side. A table for those who can't repay. Every one of them asks a person to take the lower seat.

how: Christians practice humility in confession, in serving others, and in small habits like taking the last place in line; on Maundy Thursday some churches wash feet, remembering Jesus washing his disciples' feet.

o: believing you have no worth or gifts at all
choosing the lower seat and putting others first
staying silent so that nobody notices you

games.q: the lower seat — tap the pairs.
p: the best seats at the feast

s: humility in the Bible means believing you're worthless
the guest who sits lower is still called friend; humility is the lower seat, chosen freely.
Jesus' parable about seats was told at a dinner
he watched guests choosing out the chief rooms, and told them to sit lower.
in 1 Peter, humility is pictured as something worn
be clothed with humility: put on, like clothing.

games.q: at a family dinner, your uncle tells a story and gets one small detail wrong. it doesn't matter to anyone. what fits the lower seat?
o: let him tell it his way, and enjoy the story.
correct him gently; truth matters even in small things.
correct him later, privately, so he gets it right next time.
games.why: in lowliness of mind, esteem other better: a detail nobody needs can stay his. truth in love is for what matters.

practice: Sit a little lower than usual, shoulders loose, head slightly bowed, hands resting open. Hold that posture through the sit, and bring to mind one small disagreement where you could let the other person be right.
If you pray, you can use Peter's words: God giveth grace to the humble.

wordCard.voice: Humility. Lowliness worn like clothing: the lower seat, chosen freely, with room left for someone else.

orig.note: Greek: lowliness of mind, humility. the word in 1 Peter 5:5 and Philippians 2:3.

carryVoice: Your line: clothed in humility, put on fresh each morning. Two weeks of the world, done.
